To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
teacher personality is associated with teacher support and student self efficacy but not with academic achievement.

teacher conscientiousness is positively associated with teacher academic support, teacher agreeableness is positively associated with student personal support and teacher neuroticism is negatively associated with student performance self efficacy, and that these effects are stronger for student than for teacher reports of teacher personality.

teacher personality is associated with student outcomes, and that teacher personality is more strongly associated with teacher effectiveness when measured by student reports rather than teacher self reports.
In summary, our research is concerned with
teacher noncognitive factors and teacher effectiveness.
the role of teachers' personality in the educational process.
the relationship between teacher personality and teacher effectiveness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
personality matters in the classroom.
teacher personality is an important but not sufficient predictor of teacher effectiveness.
teacher personality predicts teacher support and student self efficacy but not academic achievement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
personality is a useful construct to understand teachers' effectiveness and to improve teacher training programs in the future.
teacher personality predicts teacher effectiveness, which in turn predicts student outcomes.
teachers' personality is an important aspect of teacher effectiveness, which can be measured in a valid and reliable manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
teachers' personality traits may be an important factor to consider in the process of teacher selection.
personality matters for teacher effectiveness, and this should be considered when designing teacher training programs.
teachers' personality traits are related to their students' outcomes, especially to students' subjective perceptions of teacher support and their performance self efficacy.
